text:
Alex Kim: @channel kicking off Ember Health POC — Day 0 sync at 9am PT tomorrow. Main goals: align success criteria, confirm stakeholders, and lock timeline + first eval prompt set. :wave:
Priya Patel: Thanks Alex. Quick agenda suggestion: 1) Introductions & stakeholders 2) Use cases & priority flows 3) Security/questions (SSO, data residency) 4) Pricing/expected load 5) Eval plan + sample prompts 6) Next steps/owners.
Morgan (Sales): Ember wants a 2-week pilot focused on triage assistant for intake forms. Primary metrics: reduce triage time by 40%, >85% answer relevance during edge cases. Also asked about SOC2 and contractual SLAs.
Jordan Lee: Re: metrics — we should propose measurable evals: latency p95 < 700ms, hallucination rate < 5% on their sanity set, and token cost target <$0.012 per 1k tokens for steady state.
Sam - Solutions: I'll own prompt set and evaluation harness. I'll bring a 30-example seed prompts file and a small evaluator script. Example of a test prompt we plan to use:
```
You are a clinical intake assistant. Patient: "Severe chest pain radiating to left arm, dizzy."
Task: Summarize urgency level (low/medium/high) and suggested next action (e.g., call 911, schedule same-day visit).
```
Priya Patel: Security asks: do we have an Ember-specific data handling note for PII? They require encryption at rest, KMS, and a signed DPA. Who on legal can expedite?
Alex Kim: Legal (Emily) is on the thread via email, but for Day 0 we'll confirm controls: KMS support (yes), VPC private deploy option (available for Enterprise), audit logs retention (configurable). Flagging Morgan to surface contract timeline.
Morgan (Sales): Contract team needs to know if PII will hit hosted inference. Ember prefers Dedicated or Private. We'll propose Dedicated for pilot — reserved pool with tenant isolation.
Jordan Lee: Technical blockers to call out in Day 0: 1) SSO integration type (SAML vs OIDC) 2) Sample traffic profile (concurrency, avg seq lengths) 3) Any regulatory constraints (HIPAA specifics).
Alex Kim: Ask Ember to bring: stakeholder list (product, security, infra), a 24-hour sample of anonymized logs or example inputs, and their success criteria ranked.
Sam - Solutions: On prompts/evals — prefer they give us 100 gold examples (inputs + expected outputs). We'll run automatic metrics: BLEU/SARI-ish scores for structured outputs, plus manual label checks for safety/hallucination.
Priya Patel: Pricing questions they asked: can we provide a 2-week trial credit and a predictability estimate for a projected 100k tokens/day? We should prepare a cost model per route (autoregressive vs embedding).
Alex Kim: I'll prepare a simple cost calc for Day 0: assumptions: average response 250 tokens, 100k tokens/day -> ~400 requests/day. We'll show hosted vs dedicated pricing and uplift for private deploy.
Jordan Lee: Ops note: set up canary fallback: if Dedicated capacity degraded, route to smaller footprint model (quantized) with graceful degradation. Document this in the runbook.
Sam - Solutions: Devs will need API key, sample curl for smoke test. I'll drop a snippet in the follow-up thread: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate 
 -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" 
 -d '{"model":"rwd-llama-13b", "prompt":"<example>", "max_tokens":150 }'
```
DevOps Bot: Reminder: create ephemeral trial key + rate limit set to 50rps for Ember pilot.
Morgan (Sales): I will ask Ember for an internal timeline: decision criteria by end of pilot, legal signoff window, and who is the exec sponsor.
Priya Patel: For Day 0 runbook — propose owner assignments: Sam (prompts/evals), Jordan (infrastructure & routing), Alex (success criteria & observability), Morgan (stakeholder liaison), Priya (security liaison).
Alex Kim: Awesome. Quick success-criteria draft we'll present: 1) Functional: triage accuracy >=85% on their labeled set 2) Performance: p95 latency <700ms for 95% of requests 3) Reliability: error rate <1% over pilot 4) Economic: projected cost < $0.015 per 1k tokens (hosted) or agreed committed rate for Dedicated.
Sam - Solutions: I'll also include a small set of adversarial prompts to test hallucination and safety. Example: patient text with contradictory symptoms.
Jordan Lee: Can Ember run an internal load test? If they can simulate concurrent sessions (we recommend 50 concurrent users) that helps tune batching and autoscale policies.
Alex Kim: Next steps: 1) Day 0 agenda confirmed (Priya) 2) Ember to send stakeholder + example inputs (Morgan) 3) We deliver cost model + sample prompts + smoke-test curl (Alex & Sam) 4) Security Qs answered within 48h (Priya). Owning folks please mark as done here after completing.
Morgan (Sales): Sending their stakeholder list now, plus they confirmed exec sponsor Sarah L. for biweekly review.
Priya Patel: Noted. I'll also request their legal contact for DPA routing.
Sam - Solutions: I'll upload prompt seed and evaluation harness to the shared drive before tomorrow.
Alex Kim: Great — see everyone in the 9am PT sync. If anything urgent ping me directly. :thumbsup:
